outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 12:57 p.m. EET Tuesday, said Russian attacks on Nov 17 left some consumers without power in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Chernihiv, and Chernivtsi regions, and that emergency power cuts were also being implemented in the Kirovohrad, Poltava, and Sumy regions because of significant damage to equipment. Ukrenergo said that in some regions, through the end of the day, power-consumption restrictions would remain in place for industrial consumers and scheduled hourly power cuts affecting one to three groups would remain in place for all categories of consumers. It did not give customer counts for those regions. Earlier Tuesday, Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 11:24 a.m. EET, had listed the same nine regions as having some consumers without power, said the situation was extremely difficult in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia, where Russia has been continuously attacking energy facilities in the Dnipro region since last week, and said air-raid alerts were delaying repairs and that restored facilities were being attacked again. At that hour, the ministry said emergency outages were being applied in the Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Poltava, and Kharkiv regions because of equipment damage and reduced voltage on the high-voltage network, and that hourly outage schedules were in effect in most regions of the country, with capacity-restriction schedules for industry. Before those morning attacks, Ukrenergo had already said planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock on Tuesday, Nov 17, in parts of Ukraine: capacity-restriction schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules of 1 to 3 groups (queues) for all categories of consumers, because of the aftermath of attacks on the energy system. LB.ua, citing Ukrenergo, published that schedule update at 10:18 p.m. EET Monday. UNN, citing Ukrenergo in an 8:07 p.m. EET Monday report, said one group equals four hours without electricity, so Tuesday's scheduled outages may last from 4 to 12 hours; it said up-to-date schedules should be checked on each region's distribution-system operator. DTEK said new Tuesday-morning strikes left 700,000 households without power in Dnipropetrovsk region (see the separate Dnipro row). In Zaporizhzhia and the region, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo reported a mass outage around 8:00 a.m. EET Tuesday; as of 2:00 p.m. EET, the company said it had re-energized critical infrastructure and a significant portion of residents and legal entities, but had to suspend restoration work because of the threat of further attacks, and that work would continue until supply was fully restored. It gave no customer count for the remaining Tuesday outage (see the separate Zaporizhzhia row). Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian strikes late Monday on the city's North and South bridges over the Dnipro, and on some other infrastructure, caused some water and power cuts, traffic restrictions, and partial damage to the subway; Reuters reported that account on Tuesday. No official customer count for the Kyiv power cuts was found. DTEK Kyiv Regional Power Grids said a Tuesday attack hit an energy facility in the Boryspil district of Kyiv region, damaging equipment, and that crews were waiting for permission from the State Emergency Service and the military before inspecting the site; TrueUA published that account at 5:23 p.m. EET Tuesday, citing DTEK's official channel. DTEK Kyiv Regional Power Grids later said emergency outages that had been applied in parts of the Boryspil and Brovary districts on Ukrenergo's order were cancelled as of 2:25 p.m. EET Tuesday, and that stabilization outage schedules were again in effect in the region, according to kyivshchyna.info, which cited that 2:25 p.m. update and said the emergency cuts had lasted at least 30 minutes. No official customer count for those Kyiv-region emergency cuts was found. On Monday evening, Nov 16, Ukrenergo said enemy strikes had caused large-scale power outages in eastern Ukraine and that the situation was particularly difficult in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Poltava, and Zaporizhzhia. DTEK said the city of Dnipro was completely without power Monday evening after an attack on energy facilities in the region; as of 7:27 a.m. EET Tuesday, before the later Tuesday-morning strikes, Dnepr.info, citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, said electricity had been restored for some residents, with emergency outages still in effect in parts of Dnipro and nearby districts (see the separate Dnipro row). DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 on its facilities in the north of Odesa region left 52,200 households without power (see the separate Northern Odesa region row). No later official restoration figure for that outage was found. Overnight Nov 15, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack left 41,000 customers without power in the Odesa region, including Chornomorsk (see the separate Odesa region row). No later official restoration figure was found. In a Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; it said repairs would take time and gave no restoration time. That 3,300-customer figure is for the overnight Nov 17 southern attack and is not a later official count for the earlier northern or Chornomorsk outages. The Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration said a Monday-evening Shahed-238-type drone attack left 76 settlements in the Pervomaiskyi district without electricity; Mezha, citing a regional administration briefing as of 7:30 a.m. EET Tuesday, said electricity had been restored to all 76 settlements. Cherkasyoblenergo, in an 8:58 p.m. EET Nov 16 statement, said consumers in the Uman district were without power and that hourly outage schedules there temporarily did not apply; it gave no customer count, and no later official Uman restoration figure was found. On the Nov 15 Zaporizhzhia attack, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine, said electricity supply to 359,000 consumers was disrupted and was later restored that day; a Monday afternoon attack again substantially limited supply in the city, and the company said the situation had been stabilized by the end of Monday, with three-queue hourly schedules for the population, before Tuesday morning's mass outage. Sumyoblenergo, in a Nov 16 update reported by SUMYTODAY, said part of Sumy region was still without a stable electricity supply for a second day after an accident at a high-voltage facility (no customer count); Ukrenergo on Tuesday afternoon listed Sumy among regions with some consumers de-energized and among those under emergency cuts, without a new customer count. On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found, though both the Energy Ministry on Tuesday morning and Ukrenergo on Tuesday afternoon listed Chernihiv among regions where some consumers were de-energized, without a count. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the Odesa region; that weekly total does not give a later official figure for the morning Nov 16 or overnight Nov 15 Odesa outages. In Russian-occupied parts of the Donetsk region, occupation authorities said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity on Monday evening, that most previously de-energized consumers had been reconnected by Tuesday morning, and that forced temporary outages were again in effect Tuesday evening because of a capacity shortage and high grid load (see the separate occupied Donetsk region row).

outages.cause: New Russian attacks on energy infrastructure on the morning of Nov 17, after earlier Nov 16 attacks on energy facilities in the region
outages.affected: 700,000 households without power in Dnipropetrovsk region after new Russian strikes on the morning of Tuesday, Nov 17, according to DTEK. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power. It said the outages affected residents of Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts, that crews were first restoring power to critical infrastructure, and that work was continuing wherever the security situation allowed. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohrad, Kamianske, and Samarivka districts. No official restoration time was given. This is a later, separate wave of outages from Monday evening, Nov 16, when DTEK, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 6:59 p.m. EET and Ukrinform at 7:08 p.m. EET, said that after an attack on energy facilities in the region, the city of Dnipro was completely without power, and that some residents of the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, and Kamianskyi districts were also without electricity. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov, in a Monday Telegram post reported by NV at 7:10 p.m. EET, said that after Russian attacks on the city, almost half of Dnipro was without electricity, and he called it the sixth blackout in two weeks. He also said two people were killed, eight were in hospital, and 10 apartment buildings were damaged. As of 7:27 a.m. EET Tuesday, before the later Tuesday-morning strikes, Dnepr.info, citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, said electricity had been restored for some residents, but that scheduled stabilization outages had not yet been introduced in the hardest-hit areas, and that emergency outages remained in effect, by Ukrenergo order, in parts of the cities of Dnipro, Kamianske, and Samar, as well as in the Samarivskyi and Dniprovskyi districts, Pavlohrad and the Pavlohrad district, and Solone and Tsarychanka, while scheduled stabilization outages were in effect in the rest of the region. Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 10:14 a.m. EET Tuesday, said crews had repaired equipment overnight but that new Russian attacks again caused damage and widespread outages, so restoration work had to start again. No later official customer count or time for full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found.
outages.start: Morning of Nov 17, 2026 (Kyiv time), after earlier attacks on the evening of Nov 16

outages.affected: No official customer count for the Tuesday outage or for how many remained without power after the 2:00 p.m. EET update. Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, as reported by Inform.zp.ua at 6:30 p.m. EET Tuesday, said that as of 2:00 p.m. EET Tuesday, energy workers had re-energized critical infrastructure and a significant portion of the population and legal entities, but were forced to suspend restoration work because of the threat of repeated enemy attacks. The company's press service said work would resume as soon as the danger subsided and would continue until electricity supply was fully restored. That update came after the company's earlier Tuesday plan to fully restore supply in the city by 2:00 p.m. EET if there were no new attacks; no later official statement confirming full restoration of the city or the rest of the region was found. Earlier Tuesday, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo spokesperson Zoreslava Tsuprenko, in a comment to Ukrinform published at 11:12 a.m. EET, said that around 8:00 a.m. Tuesday, damage to energy infrastructure from systematic attacks caused a mass outage in the city of Zaporizhzhia and Zaporizhzhia region, and that as of 10:00 a.m., critical infrastructure had been re-energized. Company head Andriy Stasevskyi, as cited by Interfax-Ukraine at 11:24 a.m. EET and Inform.zp.ua at 9:06 a.m. EET, said crews were working to restore supply, that the situation was under control, that a response plan for systemic grid accidents had been introduced, and that a significant number of consumers in the city and region were de-energized. Inform.zp.ua, citing Stasevskyi, also said that on Saturday and Sunday the occupiers struck local energy facilities eight times, with about 50 grid damages recorded, and that crews had overcome the largest outage in half a year in 12 hours, returning power to more than 445,000 consumers, before the new Nov 17 attacks forced restoration work to start again. The company also said that around 4:00 p.m. Monday, another attack had substantially limited electricity supply in Zaporizhzhia, with widespread cases of unstable voltage and emergency outages, and that by the end of Monday brigades had stabilized the situation and leveled voltage, with three-queue hourly outage schedules in effect for the population. On Nov 15, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine, said electricity supply to 359,000 consumers in Zaporizhzhia and the region was disrupted and that power was later returned to 359,000 households and legal entities the same day.
outages.start: Around 8:00 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026, according to Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, after earlier attacks on Nov 15 and Nov 16
outages.etr: Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo said as of 2:00 p.m. EET Tuesday (6:00 AM CT) that a significant portion of residents and legal entities had been re-energized but that restoration work had been suspended because of the threat of further attacks, and that work would continue until supply was fully restored. No later official restoration time was given for the city or the rest of the region.

outages.cause: Russian attack on DTEK energy facilities
outages.affected: 52,200 households without power, according to a Nov 16 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 hit its energy facilities in the north of Odesa region, that 52,200 households were temporarily left without electricity, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment in order to begin repairs as soon as possible, and that all work is being carried out under safety rules, including during air-raid alerts. DTEK also said the company's production site was damaged in the attack (windows blown out and ceilings and doors damaged) and that employees were not injured. No restoration time was given. This is a separate, later attack in the north of the region from DTEK's Nov 14 statement that a morning attack on one of its facilities there left almost 50,000 customers without power, and from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. In a separate Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; that figure is for the southern Nov 17 attack and is not a later official count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that weekly total does not give a later official figure for this morning Nov 16 outage. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found after the morning Nov 16 statement.

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: 41,000 customers without power, according to a Nov 15 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack overnight on Nov 15 hit one of its energy facilities, that 41,000 customers were left without electricity, that crews began work once it was safe, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment, clearing rubble, and making repairs, that restoration will take a long time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work. No restoration time was given. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk; reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power and that six people were injured. This is a separate outage from the morning Nov 16 DTEK attack in the north of Odesa region that left 52,200 households without power. In a separate Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; that figure is for the southern Nov 17 attack and is not a later official count or restoration notice for this overnight Nov 15 outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that weekly total covers Nov 9-15 and does not give a later official figure for this overnight Nov 15 outage. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found.

outages.place: Mariupol, Donetsk, Volnovakha, Novoazovsk, and nearby cities
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. On Nov 15, the Russia-appointed head of the Donetsk occupation government, Andrey Chertkov, said the grid was damaged by a "powerful enemy attack," while some Russian media called it an accident. Vedomosti reported that Ukrainian forces struck energy infrastructure in the region overnight Nov 15. Later Tuesday, occupation authorities attributed renewed forced outages to a shortage of available capacity and high grid load
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:31 p.m. local Nov 17 report citing the occupation energy ministry, said forced temporary outages were in effect because of a shortage of available capacity and high load on the power system, measures it said were needed to prevent equipment overload and possible accidents. As of 8:00 p.m., it said partial outages affected Donetsk, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Mariupol, Makiivka, Torez, Khartsyzk, and Dokuchaievsk, as well as the Yasynuvata, Shakhtarsk, Telmanove, Amvrosiivka, and Volodarske municipal districts. The ministry said that if conditions were favorable, grid load was expected to stabilize by the end of the day, after which supply would be restored to consumers in stages. It did not give a customer count in that evening update. Earlier Tuesday, news-donetsk.ru, in a 9:09 a.m. local Nov 17 report citing occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin and Donetskenergo (a branch of JSC Yugo-Zapadnaya ESK), said that because permissible network load had been exceeded, 122 transformer substations were de-energized in the Kirovsky and Leninsky districts of Donetsk and that 23,200 subscribers remained without electricity, with restoration work under way. News-donetsk.ru, in an 8:14 a.m. local Tuesday report citing the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, said energy workers had carried out the necessary restoration work and that most previously de-energized consumers had already been reconnected. It said the regional power system remained under strain, that because of a shortage of available capacity and high grid load, forced temporary outages were possible in Donetsk, Horlivka, and Yasynuvata, and that local outages were also occurring in Makiivka, Yenakiieve, Novoazovsk, and Shakhtarsk municipal districts. It said the outages were emergency in nature, were not planned in advance, and were introduced based on the current state of the grids and the load; it did not give a new customer count. RIA Novosti's Prime, in a Tuesday report citing the same ministry Telegram statement, likewise said most previously de-energized consumers had been reconnected and that the system remained under strain, without a new customer count. Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:30 p.m. local Nov 16 report, citing the occupation administration of the head and government of the occupied Donetsk region and Donetskenergo director Oleg Pavlyak, said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity. Of those, it said 284,000 were de-energized because of the emergency shutdown of a power unit, and 144,000 household consumers were under a temporary capacity-limitation schedule (GVO) of 95 MW. It said the unit was expected to start by midnight, after which specialists planned to begin restoring supply to consumers in Donetsk, Mariupol, and the Novoazovsk, Volnovakha, and Novotroitsk districts. Earlier Monday morning figures, which have been superseded by the later Monday evening and Tuesday updates, included 201,220 subscribers without electricity in all districts of Donetsk, according to occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin citing Donetskenergo, as reported by news-donetsk.ru at 10:55 a.m. local Nov 16, and more than 133,500 subscribers without electricity in Mariupol, with 941 transformer substations in the urban district still de-energized, according to the occupation administration of the Mariupol urban district as reported by MRPL.NEWS at 9:41 a.m. local Nov 16. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed.
outages.etr: The occupation energy ministry, as reported by DAN at 8:31 p.m. local Tuesday (11:31 AM CT), said that if conditions were favorable, grid load was expected to stabilize by the end of the day, after which supply would be restored to consumers in stages. It did not give a firm restoration time or a new customer count.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Tuesday bulletin, published by Cubadebate, said that unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance; thermal generation was also limited by 426 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Tuesday bulletin, published by Cubadebate, is the latest official national forecast found: 1,730 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,050 MW available versus 2,750 MW demand (1,700 MW deficit), if the forecast conditions hold. At 6:00 a.m. Tuesday, the grid had 1,050 MW available versus 2,175 MW of demand, leaving 1,130 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,200 MW affected at midday. On Monday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Monday affectation was 1,849 MW at 7:00 p.m. Monday. Monday solar photovoltaic output was 4,284 MWh, with a maximum of 666 MW at midday. The Tuesday bulletin no longer listed the Antonio Guiteras unit or unit 1 of CTE Felton among units in breakdown or maintenance; CiberCuba, in a Monday report, said the Antonio Guiteras plant synchronized with the National Electric System on Monday after five days of emergency repairs, after going offline on Wednesday, Nov 11. CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, said that at 6:01 a.m. Tuesday La Habana reported 36 distribution circuits affected by a deficit, with 89 MW affected, and that at 3:00 a.m. Tuesday it had reported 44 circuits and 110 MW affected; the utility also reported overnight restorations on circuits C16, H443, OP319, and GC14. No later official Tuesday afternoon national actual or Havana circuit update was found. On Monday evening, CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de Las Tunas, said the province was disconnected from the National Electric System at 6:02 p.m. Monday because of a system emergency; it did not give a customer count or a reconnection time, and no later official reconnection notice was found. Official UNE and Cubadebate sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid.

outages.place: Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Pageview, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. SABC News, in a 10:01 a.m. SAST Monday, Nov 16 report, quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena saying that restoration shortly after midnight had brought several critical customers and sections of the network back online, including the SABC and Netcare Garden City Hospital, and that restoration work was continuing. He said parts of Crown remained outstanding and were scheduled to receive attention on Monday, and that technicians were also attending to further cable faults affecting customers in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Homestead Park, and Pageview, among others. eNCA, in a noon SAST Monday report attributing the update to City Power, said electricity had been restored to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and approximately half of Crown's industrial area, that residents and businesses in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, and Pageview remained without electricity because of ongoing cable faults, and that power to Sentech remained switched off for further maintenance and safety checks. No official restoration time for the remaining areas or for Sentech was given. Earlier Monday, City Power's Hursthill SDC bulletin issued at 7:30 a.m. SAST did not list the Mayfair Substation 16-hour emergency shutdown among current outages. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation; the planned window would have run until 4:00 a.m. SAST Monday. The same Monday 7:30 a.m. Hursthill bulletin said the centre was managing 1,524 open calls, 1,266 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). It also reported other Hursthill-area outages, including an investigation in Coronationville, Westbury, Newclare, and Paarlshoop (reported Sunday, no customer count); the Roosevelt Substation (Emmarentia Distributor) outage, about 75% restored, with customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield remaining off until repairs were complete; and Industria Substation outages. In a 7:35 a.m. SAST Monday Roodepoort SDC bulletin, City Power said one load centre at Florida Substation would remain off until repairs were completed for customers in Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia, and that loadshedding remains suspended until further notice. No later official City Power restoration notice for the remaining Mayfair-area suburbs, parts of Crown, or Sentech was found after the Monday midday reports.
outages.etr: No official restoration time was given for remaining Mayfair-area customers, parts of Crown, or Sentech. For the Roosevelt Substation outage in parts of Emmarentia, City Power said Monday morning that repairs were scheduled that morning and that customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield would remain off until repairs were complete. For the Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia outage, City Power said Monday morning that one load centre would remain off until repairs were completed and gave no restoration time.

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
